_doc: Per-page metadata for the Category-26 (Peptides, SARMs, and Research Chemicals) standard renderer (tools/build-category-standard-pages.mjs). Numbers come from data/standards/cat26-compiled/<record>.json (deterministic; no authored values). Display + wiring + the category _meta block only.

_meta.methodology_version: Method v2.0 — no-regulatory-anchor control form (no sovereign product limit exists; every analyte tested under mandatory control)
method_prose: No government sets a heavy-metal content limit for this class. Peptides, SARMs, and research chemicals are sold outside any drug-approval or dietary-supplement framework, so the sovereign maximum-level lookup that anchors every other HMTc standard returns nothing here. HMTc does not answer that gap by inventing a number. Every analyte on the panel is placed under mandatory control — measured on every lot by validated ICP-MS with reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation — and escalated against route-appropriate toxicological anchors (ICH Q3D / USP <232> permitted daily exposures), which flag a lot for investigation and are never used as a product-content ceiling.

Certification here is heavy-metal safety only. HMTc does not endorse, approve, or vouch for the efficacy or the legality of these products; the mark speaks solely to the heavy-metal content measured on the tested lot against the panel. Where the chemistry rules an analyte out of the matrix entirely, it is recorded as a substantiated not-material determination rather than a control.
